_comment: Every number the agents reason from, with its source. verify:true = no source found yet; don't trust it. Code.gs TARGETS mirrors this file.

water_mm_per_week.source: University of Minnesota Extension, Growing radishes: 'If the planting does not get one inch of rain each week, soak the soil thoroughly at least once a week.' https://extension.umn.edu/vegetables/growing-radishes

soil_pct.note: No published source can give these, because the % is this sensor's own dry-air-to-water scale, not soil water content. Set them from your soil during the dry run. What sources do say: keep soil 'uniformly moist ... but not wet' (Penn State PlantVillage, https://plantvillage.psu.edu/topics/radish/infos); 'uneven moisture can cause radishes to crack or split' (UMN Extension, above).

dli_mol_per_m2_day.source: C. Currey (Iowa State), greenhouse hydroponic radish DLI trial: root diameter peaked at 12-15 mol/m2/d; cracked roots rose above 15. Summarized in Greenhouse Grower, https://www.greenhousegrower.com/?p=165409. Caveat: greenhouse cultivars 'Crunchy King' and 'Red Castle', not outdoor Cherry Belle.

temp_c.optimal_source: Penn State PlantVillage: 'the optimum temperature for the growth of radishes is between 10 and 18°C (50-65°F).' https://plantvillage.psu.edu/topics/radish/infos
temp_c.bolt_note: No authoritative source gives a bolting temperature. Texas A&M AgriLife says radishes prefer 40-70°F (4-21°C) (https://aggie-horticulture.tamu.edu/vegetable/files/2011/10/radish.pdf); gardening sites say they bolt above 80°F (27°C). 25 sits between those two, unsourced.

stage_days.source: Germination: 'Seedlings will emerge within ten days' (UMN Extension, above). End of season: Cherry Belle matures in 24 days (Botanical Interests, https://botanicalinterests.com/product/Cherry-Belle-Radish-Seeds); radish harvest 20-35 days after planting (Texas A&M, above).
stage_days.note: The day-15 split between leaf growth and bulbing has no source. It doesn't change anything today, because both stages use the same soil band.

lux_to_ppfd_sunlight_factor.source: Apogee Instruments PPFD-to-lux table, 'Sunlight | 54' (https://www.apogeeinstruments.com/conversion-ppfd-to-lux/), from Thimijan & Heins 1983, HortScience 18:818-822.
